title: Private deployment messaging — Regulated buyers FAQ & positioning (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a tactical messaging & FAQ draft for Go-to-Market (SDR/AE/SE) and product marketing focused on regulated buyers evaluating Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem). It consolidates recommended control plane language, short positioning lines for different personas, common buyer objections with rebuttals, and a simple decision checklist to accelerate evaluation cycles.

Audience:
- Sales (SDR / AE) needing short talk tracks
- Solutions Engineers for demo narratives
- Product marketing for one-pagers and sales enablement

TL;DR (elevator bullets)
- Redwood Private gives you a customer-controlled inference plane: compute runs in your VPC/air-gapped network, while a lightweight control plane (optionally self-hosted) manages model lifecycle, telemetry, and rollouts.
- Designed for regulated workloads: data residency, KMS/HSM keys, audit logs, and hardened networking by default.
- We balance security and operational velocity: most customers adopt the hosted control plane + private VPC peering model for speed, and move to a self-hosted control plane only if required by policy.

Key positioning statements (short):
- For Security Leaders: "Run inference in your network, own your keys, and keep an immutable audit trail — Redwood handles runtime optimizations without lifting your data out."
- For Platform/Infra: "Plug our runtime into your cluster or VPC; we respect your identity provider, KMS, and network policies so you operate like any other internal service."
- For Procurement/Legal: "We support SOC2-ready artifacts, SC-validated data flow diagrams, and contractual commitments for data isolation and retention."

Control plane language (recommended phrasings)
- "Customer-controlled control plane": Use when buyer wants final authority. Explainer: "You choose hosted vs. self-hosted control plane. Hosted control plane orchestrates your private runtime through secure management channels; self-hosted runs entirely on your infrastructure."
- "Management plane vs. data plane": Always call out separation. "Management/control plane handles model meta-data, deployments, and metrics; inference data (inputs/outputs and KV cache) never leaves your sanctioned compute unless you opt-in."
- "Least-privilege deployment": "The control channel uses mutual TLS and explicit service identities; only authorized operators can push model versions or change routing policies."

Recommended short diagram caption (for slides or one-pager)
"Customer VPC (compute) ← secure gRPC/ mTLS channel → Redwood control plane (hosted or self-hosted). Customer keys, data, and traffic remain in VPC. Control plane sends signed deployment instructions; runtime pulls model artifacts from a customer-approved storage endpoint."

Common buyer objections & rebuttals
1) "We can’t allow any third-party control plane touching our infra."
 - Rebuttal: "Totally understood. We offer a self-hosted control plane that runs in your environment and requires zero egress. If you want hosted for faster onboarding, we provide an audited, least-privilege channel and an option to bring-your-own-tunnel (BYOT) with customer-managed certificates."
2) "What about secrets & keys?"
 - Rebuttal: "Keys live in your KMS/HSM. Our runtime only receives short-lived signing tokens and never stores long-term secrets. We integrate with common KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, HashiCorp Vault) and support HSM-backed keys for signing and encryption."
3) "How do we verify auditability and tamper evidence?"
 - Rebuttal: "We produce immutable audit logs, signed by the control plane and optionally forwarded to your SIEM. The self-hosted control plane writes logs to customer-controlled storage; hosted control plane logs can be exported to a customer-owned destination on demand."
4) "Latency & performance concerns for on-prem inference."
 - Rebuttal: "Inference runs entirely on your GPUs/CPUs inside your network. Our serving runtime optimizes kernels, batching, and KV cache management locally. The control plane only sends lightweight control signals — negligible runtime impact."
5) "Compliance/regulatory proof points?"
 - Rebuttal: "We provide compliance packs: data flow diagrams, SOC2 artifacts, pen test summary, and example configuration templates for FedRAMP-like isolation. We also offer an on-prem install validation engagement from our professional services team."
6) "Who is responsible for security updates to the runtime?"
 - Rebuttal: "For hosted runtime, Redwood manages patching per SLA. For self-hosted deployments, we provide signed releases, CVE advisories, and an optional managed-updates agent that you can approve via your change control."

Persona-specific talk tracks (30–90 second scripts)
- Security Lead (30s): "We keep inference inside your VPC and keys in your KMS. The management/control plane only issues signed deployment commands and can be self-hosted to eliminate egress. We provide audit logs and compliance artifacts you can map to your control objectives."
- Platform Engineer (45s): "The runtime is a containerized service with a small footprint, supports your identity provider and KMS, and exposes Prometheus metrics and traces. You control model rollout policies and can pin model variants to hardware profiles."
- Line of Business / Product PM (30s): "You get consistent generation quality across environments, predictable latency, and can enforce cost controls (batching/quantization) to meet product SLAs while keeping data in-house."

Competitive differentiation (how to position against two archetypes)
- Against cloud-managed AI endpoints (fast onboarding but limited isolation): "Cloud endpoints are simple but often require data to leave your environment or depend on vendor KMS. Redwood Private offers the same developer ergonomics (API, rollouts, telemetry) while keeping compute and data under your control."
- Against pure open-source self-hosting (you build everything): "Rolling your own requires ops and constant tuning for latency and cost. Redwood provides a production-hardened runtime, kernel/quantization expertise, and ops tooling so you can run securely without rebuilding inference orchestration."

Decision checklist for buyers (quick evaluation gates)
- Data residency: Yes / No — can all inference data stay in customer network?
- Key management: Does solution integrate with buyer KMS/HSM?
- Auditability: Are logs exportable to SIEM and tamper-evident?
- Patch model: Who patches runtime and how long to approve updates?
- Network policy: Is egress allowed or do we require self-hosted control plane?

Sample AE email (short)
Subject: Secure on-prem inference + audit logs — quick ask
Hi <Name>,
We’ve helped teams in financial services and healthcare run private inference with customer-controlled keys and full audit trails. Can we schedule 20 minutes to walk through a deployment pattern that keeps your data in your VPC and integrates with your KMS?

Objection playbook for SEs (triage)
- If the buyer flags "no third-party control plane": propose self-hosted control plane, provide architecture doc and runbook, and book a tech deep-dive.
- If the buyer flags "regulatory evidence needed": share compliance pack and suggest a short risk review call with our compliance lead + a reference from a similar industry.
- If the buyer flags "ops overhead": explain upgrade model, managed agent, and offer a managed-install engagement as a bridge.

Open questions for engineering/product (items to resolve before GA sales push)
- Provide a concise, one-page architecture diagram for both models (hosted-control-plane + private VPC vs fully self-hosted control plane) 
- Clarify default log retention for hosted control plane and fast path to export logs to customer destinations
- Finalize supported KMS/HSM vendors list and required permissions template
- Document rollback and canary semantics when control plane is customer-hosted

Next steps / immediate asks
- SE + PM alignment session (this week): validate the diagram and objection responses (owner: Priya)
- Produce a two-slide SDR/AE cheat sheet with 3 lines per persona and 3 objection responses (owner: Diego)
- Build a short demo script for self-hosted control plane install (owner: Morgan)

Appendix: quick glossary (so GTM uses consistent terms)
- Control plane / management plane: service that coordinates deployments, rollouts, metrics, policy.
- Data plane / runtime: code and compute that performs token generation and model execution, runs in customer network for Private deployments.
- Self-hosted control plane: the control plane software run inside customer infrastructure with no egress required.
- Hosted control plane: Redwood-hosted control plane used to orchestrate customer runtimes through secure, auditable channels.

End of doc.
